title: Atlas v2.1 launched, the eraser test closed, and the instrument without an atlas began on the whiteboard
set_out: Work from midnight to midnight Pacific. Two goals: launch the atlas v2.1 fit, with every before-launch item on the readiness board met; and, while box jobs ran, work the derivations on the whiteboard toward an instrument that needs no atlas (the author: KISS, physics first, derivations first).

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out
sections.lead: Each rule below was committed before it ran.

entries.title: The two donor halves (L19, decision 17)
entries.what: 328 donor units sealed into half A (171) and half B (157); 79 of 97 cells in both halves.
entries.why: Two independent halves give noise-free map statistics.

entries.title: The bounded transfer (L21)
entries.what: Designed, synthetic test MET, real check MET: L21 ADOPTED. Reopened later in the day (see the convergence work below).
entries.why: v2's straight line bends away from the sequencing scale.

entries.title: The five open conditions (L8)
entries.what: Rules fixed before any purity reading; the data step needed two runs (run 2 after loader inputs were not shipped); L8 settled: three conditional sets go to research; GSE137716 read by the decision 10 addendum after a correction (it is under decision 10).

entries.title: Final terms (L22)
entries.what: First design NOT MET: the launch stops. The transfer diagnosis found scatter between the sequencing and array cohorts. Second design (author: one curve, scatter carried, no cell removed): MET.

entries.title: Run script, planted test, dry run, cost sheet (L9, L10, L11)
entries.what: The run script, block driver and declared outputs committed; planted test MET (run 2 after a redesign); the dry run of the data assembly OK; the cost sheet written, then real prices from the author's AWS account.

entries.title: Commissioning bars (L15)
entries.what: Sealed before the atlas exists; their scorers planted-tested.
entries.why: The atlas is judged by rules set in advance.

entries.title: The eraser test (DEV-ERASE-01)
entries.what: The eraser-removed sets declared and the several-set verdict rule fixed before any read; the planted check on real molecules MET; reads run 1 stalled, run 2 by the AWS copy of SRA; unit U1 first; then all primary units read once: NOT MET. The job's verdict file was written once.
entries.why: Tests whether writing and erasing each take half of the held balance.

entries.title: Cell position from RNA (DEV-POSITION-EXPR-01)
entries.what: Committed before it ran; run once: NOT MET (rank correlation +0.101 over 30 cell types).

entries.title: Architecture against the healthy held error (DEV-ARCH-01)
entries.what: Exploration: the loosely held share tracks the held error across 56 cell types (rank correlation +0.87).

entries.title: Atlas v2.1 convergence and speed
entries.what: Block 0 ran 7 times over the cost sheet; the model did not mix on real data and the launch was held. Strict transfer design 1 NOT MET before any fit; design 2 committed; its planted test NOT MET (the flat curve is not the cause), after a false start. Diagnostics 2 to 5: the anchored transfer fixes the mixing and passes the Flatness check on 60 real loci; the smooth transfer (PCHIP) is faster, not fixed; the curve and the scatter term are not the cause; diagnostic 5 found two causes, one of them the noise taken from the converted value. Mode v21inv: planted test NOT MET (sampler bar), real check NOT MET by 0.0004 (R3).

entries.title: Atlas v2.1 fitted in mode v21inv (author decision)
entries.what: Adopted with both missed bars and the numbers that justify it: agreement 0.24 standard errors, 98.7 percent inside the exact model's interval. Block 0: B1, L18 and L23 met (79 cells distinct, r 0.9961 against v2). L12 code checksums written. The fit launched: 700 blocks, about 24 hours, about $180.

entries.title: Fit machines
entries.what: The first spot machine was reclaimed (public ledger row added; fit relaunch plan); the second fit machine was reclaimed and B1/L18 moved to the box; the fit moved to on-demand (author).
entries.why: Spot capacity for large machines was poor.

sections.heading: What we learned that we did not know yesterday

entries.title: Removing the eraser does not halve the held error
entries.what: The eraser is real but small where we count.
entries.why: Kills the per-site half-and-half as the origin of the middle line; the middle line itself stays measured.

entries.title: Fully held sites read at the writer's own limit
entries.what: On sites every cell keeps fully methylated, cells read 0.0136 to 0.0226, inside the writer limit 1/(1 + D), 0.0123 to 0.0207 (overnight whiteboard).
entries.why: An enzyme constant, the same for everyone, is a reference with no atlas.

entries.title: The island side is held at nameplate and ignores architecture
entries.what: Across 56 healthy cell types a gained mark between unmethylated neighbors reads 0.0094 to 0.0162 (29 inside the writer band, 27 just below), with no relation to the loose share. Whiteboard into the four-domain table: gate error, leakage, one reading per instrument; step 4 prepared (DEV-BACKBONE-01, not run).
entries.why: The clean side to watch for the overdrive writer.

entries.title: The cosmos
entries.what: Cosmos Mahaffey number filled from our own 2026-10-02 computation (black hole 2 ln2, horizon ln2 per bit); cosmos fidelity ratio: none for the whole universe (author); the star gauge added to the schematic (author).

sections.heading: Our own mistakes today, and what caught each

entries.title: Stem-cell names in the first half-split run
entries.what: The first run used the bare labels (HSC, CMP and so on) instead of v2's names (HSC (bone marrow) and so on).
entries.why: Caught by checking every name against the roster before sealing; fixed, no rule changed.

entries.title: Cuts that were never written
entries.what: Decisions 1 and 10 say their eosinophil and non-epithelial cuts were fixed in the plan; neither number was ever written down.
entries.why: Caught while preparing the step that reads those arrays; the cuts will be committed before any of them is read.

entries.title: The fit judged by R-hat alone
entries.what: Correction: the v2.1 fit was judged by R-hat alone, against the Flatness Lesson. The author caught it; the Flatness check became launch item L23.

entries.title: Bars set without a reason
entries.what: Lesson C15: bars in the units of their purpose (author). Two round-number bars failed good work; both verdicts stand as written.

entries.title: The retired term
entries.what: The retired term (author): the held error, not a copying error. Renamed everywhere current; push rule 26 refuses the old term.
entries.why: Two days running the copying frame came back.

entries.title: A cost quoted from a light slice
entries.what: The fit was quoted at about $45 from 60 sites lighter than a full block; block 0 measured about $180. Corrected to the author before launch.

entries.title: Our own design error in the v2.1 model
entries.what: The adopted curve's flat stretches and a finite-difference slope; recorded as an assistant design error.

entries.title: A box code check gap
entries.what: Box code check: data inputs that are another job's S3 output, now verified byte for byte.

sections.heading: Coffee and a whiteboard: how the day's ideas actually arrived

entries.title: Derivation ledger and the physics game plan
entries.what: The derivation ledger (the author asked for the full derivations); the physics game plan (author): an instrument that needs no atlas; the overnight whiteboard.

entries.title: The efficiency premise and the two ends
entries.what: The author's premise: a design holds firm what it uses. The gauge's two ends became gate error (derived) and leakage (open). The loose end waits by the author's decision; one reading per instrument.

entries.title: Derivations first, KISS
entries.what: No new data tests, searches or calibrations unless the author asks; sealed jobs already running finish.

entries.title: Use tests for Loyfer and Moss
entries.what: Showcase tests written and sealed while the fit runs, before any atlas output is opened: markers, mixtures (with a wide-area mixture of cells their atlas lacks), and the extras shown.

open_at_turnover: The atlas v2.1 fit is running (700 blocks, finishing about 11:30 PM Pacific on 2026-10-15). Next: write and seal the Loyfer and Moss use tests; steps 1 to 3 on paper before DEV-BACKBONE-01 runs; the island-side counts for the tumor pairs (not saved; recovery needs the raw files).
closing: Nine sealed or synthetic results, two NOT MET outcomes that stand as written, six of our own errors found and recorded, and the atlas fit launched on the plan's budget.
